episodes.title: Sharing the road with driverless cars
episodes.description: Imagine crossing a road and turning to see a car heading towards you... without a driver! While this might seem scary, driverless cars are already operating safely in many cities around the world. These autonomous cars contain huge amounts of technology to help them drive alongside other road users carefully. But will humans behave as carefully around them? Can we communicate clearly with these 'robotaxis', or are we simply incompatible? Phil and Pippa discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Learn English from authentic BBC programme clips. Get a free worksheet, quiz and transcript for this...
episodes.titleZh: 与无人驾驶汽车共享道路
episodes.descZh: 想象一下，过马路，转身看到一辆汽车朝你驶来……没有司机！虽然这看起来很可怕，但无人驾驶汽车已经在世界各地的许多城市安全运行。这些自动驾驶汽车包含大量技术，可以帮助它们与其他道路使用者一起小心驾驶。但人类在它们周围会表现得如此谨慎吗？我们能与这些“机器人出租车”清晰地沟通吗？还是我们根本不相容？菲尔和皮帕讨论这个问题并教你一些新词汇。从真实的BBC节目剪辑中学习英语。为此获得免费的工作表、测验和成绩单.

episodes.title: Sunday Pick: How to mentally reset when you’re stressed out (w/ Dr Jenny Taitz) | How to Be a Better Human
episodes.description: It’s hard to not feel stress at the state of the world today, so how can you cope with stressors without letting them completely overwhelm you? Clinical psychologist Jenny Taitz spends most of her days helping clients navigate through their stress. She shares why she uses Dialectical Behavior Therapy, or DBT, in her therapy work, whether a cold plunge can help you snap out of your messy ruminations, and why doing a few tasks each day to practice for pleasure and mastery can help improve your mood. Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/pr...
episodes.titleZh: 周日选择：当你压力大时如何重新调整心理（珍妮·泰茨博士）|如何成为一个更好的人
episodes.descZh: 在当今的世界中，很难不感受到压力，那么如何才能在不让它们完全压垮你的情况下应对压力源呢？临床心理学家珍妮·泰兹（Jenny Taitz）大部分时间都在帮助客户应对压力。她分享了为什么她在治疗工作中使用辩证行为疗法（DBT），寒冷的潜水是否可以帮助你摆脱混乱的沉思，以及为什么每天做一些任务来练习以获得快乐和掌握可以帮助改善你的情绪。由Acast主持。请参阅acast.com/pr..

episodes.title: Selects: How Narcolepsy Works
episodes.description: Narcolepsy is one of those amazing rare disorders that everyone thinks they understand – people just fall asleep at random times, even in the middle of doing something. But there’s a lot more to it and – even better – we actually may be able to explain it. Josh and Chuck run it down in this classic episode. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
episodes.titleZh: 警告：嗜睡症是如何起作用的
episodes.descZh: 嗜睡症是令人惊叹的罕见疾病之一，每个人都认为自己理解--人们只是在随机的时间睡着，即使是在做某事的过程中。但事情还有很多，甚至更好的是，我们实际上可能能够解释它。乔什和查克在这一经典剧集中详细说明了这一点。请访问omnystudio.com/listener了解隐私信息。

episodes.title: Is a Museum Just a Trophy Case? (Update)
episodes.description: The world’s great museums are full of art and artifacts that were plundered during an era when plunder was the norm. Now there’s a push to return these works to their rightful owners. Sounds simple, right? It's not. (Part 2 of an updated series originally published in 2023.) SOURCES: Matthew Bogdanos, assistant district attorney in the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office and chief of the Antiquities Trafficking Unit. Nicholas Cullinan, director of the British Museum. Victor Ehikhamenor, Nigerian writer and artist. David Frum, staff writer at The Atlantic. Dan Hicks, professor of contemporary archaeology at the University of Oxfo...
episodes.titleZh: 博物馆只是奖杯吗？（更新）
episodes.descZh: 世界上最伟大的博物馆里充满了在掠夺成为常态的时代被掠夺的艺术品和文物。现在，人们正在推动将这些作品归还给其合法所有者。听起来很简单，对吧？不是的(Part最初于2023年发布的更新系列中的2个。）资料来源：马修·博格达诺斯（Matthew Bogdanos），曼哈顿地区检察官办公室助理地区检察官兼文物贩运部门负责人。尼古拉斯·库里南，大英博物馆馆长。维克多·艾希卡梅诺，尼日利亚作家和艺术家。大卫·弗拉姆（David Frum），《大西洋月刊》撰稿人。牛津大学当代考古学教授丹·希克斯……

episodes.title: The English We Speak: Say less
episodes.description: This modern expression is a way of responding enthusiastically to a suggestion. It means something similar to ‘say no more’. Learn when and how to use it with Georgie and Feifei. As always, find a free transcript here: ✔️ https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/the-english-we-speak_2026/ep-260817 For more great language tips and programmes visit bbclearningenglish.com We send a newsletter with our weekly highlights - subscribe here: ✔️ https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/newsletters
episodes.descZh: 这种现代表达是对建议热情回应的一种方式。它的意思类似于“别再说了”。了解何时以及如何与乔吉和菲菲一起使用它。与往常一样，请在此处找到免费的成绩单：https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/the-english-we-speak_2026/ep-260817有关更多精彩的语言技巧和节目，请访问bbclearningenglish.com我们发送包含每周亮点的时事通讯-在此处订阅：https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/newsletters️️

episodes.description: Here it is, finally! The long-awaited episode 1000. It has taken me weeks to finish this. If you listen, you will understand why it has taken so long! This is a celebration of this podcast after 17 years and 1000 episodes. It includes a lot of rambling, an interview with my brother, questions from friends and family, and the voices of various guests who have been on this podcast over the last few years. Also, regular interruptions from my daughter and all sorts of other random moments such as the sounds of dogs, woodpeckers, neighbours, and more! Thank you to all the...
episodes.descZh: 终于到了！期待已久的第1000集我花了几个星期才完成。如果你听了，你就会明白为什么花了这么长时间！这是对这个播客17年、1000集的庆祝。其中包括很多漫无边际、对我兄弟的采访、朋友和家人的问题，以及过去几年来参加过这个播客的各种嘉宾的声音。此外，我女儿的定期打断以及各种其他随机时刻，例如狗的声音、啄木鸟的声音、邻居的声音等等！感谢所有.

episodes.title: Chatterbox #352 – Hot hot summer
episodes.description: What does a heat wave actually do to your day? Andrew and Anna compare their summers from opposite sides of the world. Anna is in Madrid, where a hot day reaches 40 degrees and the blinds stay closed until evening. Andrew is in Seoul, where the rainy season just ended but the humidity stayed. They talk about air conditioning, lost sleep, cold showers, and the wildfires that burned west of Madrid this summer. Keep an ear out for these phrases during the episode: Not so fast Respite Bar none To do one’s business Bone dry To bu...
episodes.descZh: 热浪实际上对你的一天有什么影响？安德鲁和安娜从世界两端比较了他们的夏天。安娜在马德里，炎热的天气达到40度，百叶窗一直关闭到晚上。安德鲁在首尔，那里的雨季刚刚结束，但湿度仍然存在。他们谈论空调、睡眠不足、冷水淋浴以及今年夏天在马德里西部燃烧的野火。在剧集中留意这些短语：别那么快恢复酒吧没有做自己的事骨头干为了.

episodes.title: How to Be A Better Partner
episodes.description: When we look at the people we love, how clearly do we really see them? This week, we talk with psychologist Edward LeMay about how our fears, desires, and insecurities can shape our perceptions of our partners — sometimes creating the very reality we expect. He explains how we can learn to see our partners in ways that create greater trust and connection. Then, Sonja Lyubomirsky answers your questions about the gap between being loved and feeling loved, in our latest installment of "Your Questions Answered." If you enjoy listening to Hidden Brain, we think you'll enjoy watching it...
episodes.titleZh: 如何成为更好的合作伙伴
episodes.descZh: 当我们看着我们所爱的人时，我们真正看到他们的清晰度有多高？本周，我们与心理学家爱德华·勒梅（Edward LeMay）谈论我们的恐惧、欲望和不安全感如何塑造我们对伴侣的看法--有时会创造我们所期望的现实。他解释了我们如何学会以建立更大信任和联系的方式看待我们的合作伙伴。然后，索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基（Sonja Lyubomirsky）在我们最新一期的《你的疑问》中回答了您关于被爱和感觉被爱之间差距的问题。“如果你喜欢听《隐藏的大脑》，我们认为你会喜欢看它..

episodes.title: Patient Zero
episodes.description: The greatest mysteries have a shadowy figure at the center—someone who sets things in motion and holds the key to how the story unfolds. In epidemiology, this central character is known as Patient Zero—the case at the heart of an outbreak. This hour, Radiolab digs up an episode we first produced in 2011 and hunts for Patient Zeroes from all over the map. We start with the story of perhaps the most iconic Patient Zero of all time: Typhoid Mary. Then, we dive into a molecular detective story to pinpoint the beginning of the AIDS, and we re-imagine the...
episodes.descZh: 最伟大的谜团的中心都有一个影子--一个让事情运转起来并掌握着故事如何展开的关键的人。在流行病学中，这个中心人物被称为零号病人--疫情爆发的核心病例。这一小时，Radiolab挖掘了我们于2011年首次制作的一集，并在地图上寻找Patient Zeroes。我们从可能是有史以来最具标志性的零号患者的故事开始：伤寒玛丽。然后，我们深入研究一个分子侦探故事，找出艾滋病的起源，并重新想象.

episodes.title: 100 Objects #14: Basketball Sleeve
episodes.description: Producer and reporter Ramtin Arablouei (co-creator of the NPR show, Throughline) has a simple question: why are so many NBA players wearing a compression sleeve on their arm? It seems like everyone has one. Do they all have elbow issues? The answer is really the story of Allen Iverson, an underdog player who went from a prison cell to international fame in just a few years. And through the story of him and his sleeve, you can see the whole history of basketball’s relationship with race, with respectability politics, and who gets to look like what on the co...
episodes.descZh: 制片人兼记者Ramtin Arablouei（NPR节目《Journline》的联合创始人）有一个简单的问题：为什么这么多NBA球员的手臂上戴着压缩套？似乎每个人都有一个。他们都有肘部问题吗？答案实际上是艾伦·艾弗森的故事，他是一位处于劣势的球员，在短短几年内就从监狱变成了国际知名度。通过他和他的袖子的故事，你可以看到篮球与种族、尊重政治以及谁在比赛中看起来像什么的整个历史.

Then Shirin in Texas wants to differentiate her graphic stationery in a crowded Etsy marketplace. And Mark from New Jersey works through refocusing his line of craft spirits. Plus, Carlton’s recent efforts to pass on his trendspottting talent to the next generation. episodes.title: Think Baseball Is Boring? The Savannah Bananas Are Here to Fix That.
episodes.description: Jesse and Emily Cole created theSavannah Bananaswith a simple mission in mind: to make baseball as entertaining as possible. They introduced some innovations to America’s pastime, including twerking umpires, stilt-walking pitchers and TikTok-ready choreographed dance numbers. They tinkered with the rules of baseball, making a game that was shorter and faster, with plenty of opportunities for fan engagement. The result? A sports sensation. In the 10 years since its founding, the team has become one of the most popular sports organizations in the world, reaching tens of millions of fans online, with a waiting list of millions of others ho...
episodes.titleZh: 你觉得棒球很无聊吗？萨凡纳香蕉来解决这个问题。
episodes.descZh: 杰西和艾米丽·科尔创建萨凡纳香蕉队的使命很简单：让棒球尽可能有趣。他们为美国的消遣方式引入了一些创新，包括电臀裁判、高跷投手和TikTok准备的编舞舞蹈号码。他们修改了棒球规则，制作了一款更短、更快的比赛，为球迷提供了大量参与机会。结果？体育轰动。成立10年来，该球队已成为世界上最受欢迎的体育组织之一，在网上吸引了数千万粉丝，还有数百万其他粉丝在等待.
